exposure: Implementation of a new 39-week elective induction policy
outcome: Rates of labor induction and elective induction
cohort: Live, singleton, in-born deliveries ≥36 weeks gestation (excluding fetal anomalies and prolonged antenatal admission) one year before and one year after implementation of the policy
finding: Following the implementation of a nonrestrictive, 39-week elective induction policy, rates of 39-week labor induction and elective inductions increased across all studied subgroups, while cesarean delivery rates remained unchanged, but median time from admission to delivery and cumulative admission to delivery hours increased significantly.
